title: Flora Nwapa's birth chart
metaDescription: Flora Nwapa's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 22.3° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.7° separates Mars and Uranus from an exact trine; at that range drive and disruption read as one mechanism. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 22.3° Capricorn, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Mercury. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (7.1°), Venus in Sagittarius (7.2°), Mars in Leo (12.3°): thought with its feet on the ground, attraction declared rather than implied, effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Jupiter to Saturn, an opposition with 0.6° of slack. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner. Behind it, Mars trine Uranus at 0.7°, and Mercury trine Neptune at 1.6° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Venus, Mars, Uranus close a triangle of trines. A grand trine is read as self-sufficiency in one element: the current circulates whether or not anything is asked of it. Mercury opposes Jupiter while both square Uranus. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, three placements stand out. The Moon in Scorpio at 20.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Cancer at 14.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Capricorn at 15.2° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 earth, 3 water, 3 fire by element and 6 cardinal, 2 fixed, 2 mutable by mode. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.2° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 20.3°.
